bibliography.note: Canadian Journal of Fisheries and Aquatic Sciences 49(9): 1932–1937, 1992; Wu, L. & Culver, D. A. — matches

claims.claim: young yellow perch take no benthos below 30 mm, and benthos above 50 mm when zooplankton is scarce
claims.note: the abstract says exactly this: perch < 30 mm total length 'did not consume benthic prey' in the laboratory experiments or the field, while fish > 50 mm did 'at low zooplankton densities' (western Lake Erie, June–August). Confirmation of the conditions (prey densities, sample sizes) needs the full text; the paper already marks it '(abstract)'.

claims.claim: perch > 5 cm switch to the bed when the zooplankton runs low (Wu & Culver 1992)
claims.note: consistent with the abstract (age-0 yellow perch, > 50 mm TL, at low zooplankton density); the abstract is about young-of-year perch, so applying it to all perch over 5 cm, adults included, is the project's extension.

claims.claim: adults split their foraging time among their foods in proportion to f⁴, f being each food's own functional response (after Werner et al. 1983 and Wu & Culver 1992)
claims.note: nothing in the abstract resembles an f⁴ allocation rule or a functional response: it reports a size- and zooplankton-density-dependent diet shift in AGE-0 perch. The rule looks like the project's own construction, motivated by both papers; unless the full text has it, say 'a project rule, motivated by …'.

notes: Abstract (Crossref) in brief: field studies in western Lake Erie showed age-0 yellow perch shifting from exclusively zooplankton to mainly benthic prey during June–August, coinciding with a zooplankton decline; laboratory feeding experiments tied the shift to fish size; growth declined after the zooplankton decline. The density at which the switch happens (what the project's note wanted, YW02) is not in the abstract.
